title: INT8 weight-only: stability & cross-model calibration harness for GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable integration and regression test harness that validates INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) across a representative model matrix, hardware tiers, and real-world prompts. The harness must exercise the full calibration workflow (profile collection, per-layer scale computation, optional per-channel correction), evaluate end-to-end accuracy and stability, and gate changes in CI/nightly jobs and canary rollouts.

Scope:
- Integrate existing profile generation code with a new convergence/stability pipeline that runs across multiple seeds and temperature settings.
- Add deterministic golden-eval workloads (SQuAD-like QA, summarization, generation perplexity) and metric thresholds tuned per-model family.
- Provide automated diffing for model outputs (token-level and embedding drift) and guardrails for acceptable drift.
- Hook the harness into: 1) PR-level smoke, 2) nightly regression, 3) canary rollout checks.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement of the calibration library (we will call into current GPTQ/AWQ implementations).
- Extensive per-customer profiling - this is focused on platform-level profiles and regressions.
acceptance_criteria: CI smoke job runs a minimal calibration + infer on 3 small models (MPT-7B, Llama2-13B, Falcon-7B) and fails the PR if top-line perplexity regresses beyond configured deltas.
Nightly pipeline executes a full sweep across the model matrix (sizes 7B, 13B, 30B where available) and produces a summary artifact with per-model metric deltas and seed variance statistics.
Canary check evaluates rolling percentiles over 1000 samples and blocks rollout if 95th percentile latency or 99th percentile token-level disagreement exceed thresholds.
Automated rollback playbook exists and is runnable by on-call with a single command to revert to FP32 or prior quant profile variant.
Stability test shows inter-seed variance below configured thresholds (token F1 variance < 0.8% across 5 seeds) for at least 3 model families.
Regression dashboard artifact is published to S3 and linked into the release notes; data retention follows observability policy (30 days for regtest artifacts).
test_plan: Test matrix: models {MPT-7B, Llama2-13B, Falcon-7B, Meta-Llama-2-13B (open weights)}, sequence lengths {128, 512, 2048}, batch sizes {1, 8, 32}, hardware {A100-40GB, H100-80GB}. Workloads: QA (SQuAD small subset), summarization (CNN/DailyMail subset), next-token perplexity (wikitext fragment), and an n-shot instruction set for hallucination/regression signals. Metrics: perplexity, exact match / F1, token-level edit distance, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, end-to-end latency and p50/p95/p99. Regression thresholds: model-family-specific baselines stored in the quant-profiles registry; report if delta > preconfigured tolerances. Seed stability: run 5 different RNG seeds for calibration and report mean/std. CI integration: fast-smoke (3 models, short seq) on PR; full-regression on nightly; canary checks run for any rollout to dedicated clusters.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge harness to staging branch, enable PR smoke and nightly jobs for non-critical models. Phase 2: Run full nightly for 2 weeks, tune thresholds with product/regression owners. Phase 3: Enable canary gating on dedicated clusters for small percentage of traffic (5% -> 20%). Phase 4: Promote to non-dedicated hosted API with gradual traffic ramp. Rollback triggers: metric delta exceedance OR user-facing error rate increase above 0.1%.
updates: 2025-11-02: Ticket created - initial spike completed; prototype harness that runs calibration + inference locally for a single model (MPT-7B).
2025-11-04: Discovered a noise pattern in AWQ layer-wise scales that increases perplexity on long-form sequences; opened investigation to add per-layer clipping during calibration.

2025-11-07: Added golden-seed dataset (1k examples across QA/summarize/perplexity); baseline metrics collected for three model families and uploaded to s3://redwood-quant/regressions/baselines/2025-11-07/
2025-11-09: Integration PR opened to add harness job definitions and artifacts export (https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/16842). Awaiting review from infra and QA.
2025-11-11: Nightly pipeline skeleton wired into CI; first run completed but one failure due to missing torch compile flags on H100 runner - infra ticket opened (INFRA-4221).
risks: False positives in regression detection causing unnecessary rollbacks (mitigation: tiered thresholds + manual approval for small deltas).
Hardware variance (A100 vs H100) leading to inconsistent perf regressions (mitigation: normalize metrics per-hardware and run hardware-specific baselines).
AWQ per-layer instability on certain transformer variants (mitigation: add per-layer clipping and fall back to GPTQ for flagged layers).
mitigations: Add a two-tier alert: first a soft warning reported to the regression dashboard, then a hard gate only if the 3-day rolling average exceeds thresholds.
Extend the harness to capture kernel-level telemetry and infer nondeterminism sources; share with runtime team for kernel patching.
Provide a fast fallback script in the oncall playbook to switch traffic to FP32/dedicated capacity in <10 minutes.
notes: Coordinate with runtime owners (cc: @runtime-team) to ensure kernel flags used by AWQ/GPTQ are supported on CI runners.
We should record sample-level token diffs and store them alongside aggregated metrics for debugging reproducibility issues.
Consider adding a synthetic stress mode that injects prefix caching and cross-batch KV reuse to catch batching-related regressions.
